# NPM Improved v1.6.1 — Show actual backend node hostname

## Identify the node serving the shared UI

NPMi now displays a persistent **Node: hostname** indicator in the global administration header. The hostname is the physical Docker host that **answered the most recently completed API request**, not the shared public proxy DNS name, the Docker container ID, or an NPMX-configured display name.

- API responses carry an `X-NPMi-Node-Hostname` header and disable intermediary caching of node-specific API data.
- The browser updates the indicator when any NPMi API response comes back from a different server, including when multiple nodes answer `proxy.gigabytegrove.net`. A change indicator identifies a detected switch.
- If the Linux host is not identified, the header says **Unidentified** instead of inventing a hostname.
- The current physical hostname is also shown in the Analytics Center's node banner, alongside the separate NPMX friendly name and role.
- The Analytics Center retains its multi-page reporting, investigation, IP/user-agent, connection-history and enforcement sections. Existing per-host Analytics is unchanged.

## Native host identity

The supported host-native updater installer records the real Linux hostname in the installation's **node-local** `/data/host-updater-ready.json` marker. The application checks the marker against its local project identity and reads the current hostname on every API request. On existing managed nodes, the v1.6.1 updater package refreshes this marker automatically once the native host updater receives its matching release.

Custom Linux deployments without a native host marker can explicitly set `NPM_NODE_HOSTNAME` in the Compose environment. NPMi **never** claims that Docker's automatically generated container hostname is the physical machine.

## Important shared-endpoint behavior

When the same public DNS address load-balances requests to several nodes **without sticky sessions**, individual API calls can reach different nodes. The header therefore identifies the **last API responder**, not a guaranteed permanent connection, and can change while the page is open. Node-specific analytics report responses carry their own source-node hostname to avoid mistaking one node's observations for another's.

No additional Docker containers, updater helpers or developer interfaces are introduced.
